title: Caller Offering to Answer Texts Tonight, Plus Hours Form

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Workforce Coordinator Desk, Ext. 2214

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Hi, um, is this the crisis center? The person who does staffing? Sorry, I got transferred twice. My name's Brielle Sandoval, I'm a nursing student here in Lincoln. I saw the news about Ellery Ridge and I just... I want to help.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I finished my psych rotation last month, so I've done the therapeutic communication module and everything. I'm free all night. Can I come in and answer texts? I can be there by five. I don't need to be paid or anything.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Okay. And one more thing, sorry, while I have you. I need someone to sign my volunteer service-hours form. It's 12 hours from last semester. I think your old volunteer coordinator approved it, but I can't find her email. Can you sign it this afternoon? The college portal closes at 23:59 tonight, and if it's not in, I lose the credit.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Could I just email it to you right now? It's only one signature. It'll take you like two minutes.

voiceStyles.Caller: Woman in her early 20s. Earnest, a little breathless, talking fast and apologizing. Echo from a campus hallway, with a door closing somewhere behind her.

instructorNote: This is a noise inject meant to test whether the Workforce Coordinator can say no politely and fast. Look for a reply in under a minute: thank her, explain that GPCN does not put untrained volunteers on live contacts (Staffing 6), and take her name and number so someone can follow up about the form later. Watch whether the call takes time away from the call-in list and from tracking who is confirmed for the evening shift.
